# How good is the data? {#sec-data-quality}


::: {.cell}

:::


No administrative dataset is perfect, and this one combines three. This
chapter summarises how far the CARS data can be relied on, mainly by comparing
it with DfT's official counts of vehicles. The pipeline's data quality report
([Data quality report](../reports/data_quality_report.md), in the appendices) has every check in detail.

## Comparison with DfT vehicle counts

DfT's vehicle licensing statistics count every vehicle on the DVLA register at
the end of each year, licensed or SORN. The CARS data counts the vehicles
*observed* (tested) in each year. The two should not agree exactly:

- vehicles under three have no MOT; CARS includes them once they have had
  their first test, but misses the newest ones, not yet tested;
- SORN vehicles are in DfT's count but are not tested;
- heavy goods vehicles, large buses and most historic vehicles do not take an
  MOT;
- CARS carries a vehicle's postcode area forward for about two years after
  its last MOT (@sec-lifecycle), so a vehicle scrapped or exported after its
  last test stays in the CARS count for about two years after it has left
  DfT's.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Vehicles aged three and over observed in the CARS data, as a ratio of DfT's count of licensed and SORN vehicles of the same age, by body type.](data-quality_files/figure-html/fig-dft-ratio-1.png){#fig-dft-ratio fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

:::


For cars and vans aged three and over the two sources are close. CARS counts
somewhat more cars than DfT (1.17 times as many in 2018,
1.04 in 2025), mainly because a car's postcode area is
carried forward for about two years after its last MOT, so recently scrapped
cars are still counted. Counting vehicles of *all* ages, CARS falls below DfT in the most
recent years, because vehicles first registered then have not yet been tested
(@sec-pitfalls).

Motorcycles are the exception: CARS observes a falling share of the
motorcycles on DfT's register, 0.55 of those aged three and over
in 2025. Many motorcycles are kept on SORN or used seasonally, and so are
tested irregularly.

::: {.callout-note .todo title="To be confirmed"}
Whether the falling motorcycle ratio is explained by SORN and irregular
testing, or partly by how motorcycles are classified or linked.
:::


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Vehicles of all body types by age in 2022: observed in the CARS data and counted by DfT (licensed plus SORN).](data-quality_files/figure-html/fig-dft-age-1.png){#fig-dft-age fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


By age (@fig-dft-age), the sources
agree well between about 3 and 16 years. Younger vehicles are missing from
CARS because they have not had an MOT. Older vehicles are increasingly missing
because many are kept on SORN, or are exempt from the MOT once 40 years old.

## Completeness of key fields


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

:::


| Field | Missing | Note |
|---|--:|---|
| Make (`make_final`) | 0.56% | |
| Model (`model_final`) | 4.27% | Mostly where the recorded model is a placeholder such as UNKNOWN |
| Body type | 3.13% | |
| Fuel (`fuel`) | 0% | "Other" for a small number |
| Engine size (`engine_cc`) | 0.86% | Mostly tractors and plant |
| CO~2~ (`co2`) | 25.99% | Mostly older vehicles, registered before CO~2~ was recorded |
| Euro status (`euro_status`) | 0% | Includes values assumed from the date |
| Test class (`test_class`) | 5.9% | |
| First-use date | 0% | From DVSA for 82.3%, NA% of vehicles |

## Known issues

- **The final years are incomplete.** 2025 is a partial year, and the youngest
  vehicles are missing from the last three years (@sec-pitfalls).
- **Northern Ireland** vehicles are included, but the test class is not
  supplied for them, and testing there was disrupted in 2020.
- **2005** appears to be of lower quality than later years, and some CARS
  reports start comparisons in 2006.
- **DVLA records describing another vehicle.** Where a registration has moved
  between vehicles, the DVLA record may describe the wrong one. The pipeline
  detects the clear cases and does not use their values; some subtler cases
  will remain.
- **Make and model matching** is very good for common vehicles and weaker for
  rare ones, motorcycles and specialist vehicles. `model_confidence` and
  `model_method` show how each match was made.

:::
